podcast.title: Plane Crash Death (1957)
podcast.body: On February 3, 1957, a day famously known as "the day the music died," The Big Bopper was killed when the small plane he was a passenger in went down in a cornfield outside of Mason City, Iowa. He died alongside fellow musicians Buddy Holly and Richie Valens. "February 3rd, 1957 has gone down in history as the day the music died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death in Plane Crash (1959)
podcast.body: The Big Bopper died in a plane crash on February 3, 1959, along with Buddy Holly and Richie Valens, during the "Winter Dance Party" tour. He had been suffering from the flu due to the miserable tour conditions and took Buddy Holly's chartered plane for comfort. "You're likely also to know that Richie Valens and the Big Bopper died in the same crash, even if you don't know any of the songs that either of those two artists recorded."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Last-Minute Plane Passenger (1959)
podcast.body: The Big Bopper was offered a seat on Buddy Holly's chartered plane to Fargo, North Dakota, given the harsh tour conditions and his illness, replacing Tommy Allsup or Waylon Jennings. "eventually they gave up their seats to the two other people who were suffering the most, the big bumper and valence."

podcast.title: Plane Crash Death (1959)
podcast.body: Big Wopper was killed in a small plane crash in a cornfield outside Mason City, Iowa, on February 3, 1959. This tragedy, which also claimed the lives of Buddy Holly and Ritchie Valens, is historically referred to as "the day the music died." "Buddy Holly, Richie Val, and Big Wopper were all killed when their small plane went down in a cornfield outside of Mason City, Iowa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accomplished Songwriter (Year not specified)
podcast.body: Despite being known for a novelty hit, The Big Bopper was an accomplished songwriter. "The Big Bopper, who was actually a fairly accomplished songwriter, but was touring on the basis of his one hit, a novelty song called Shantilly Lace."

podcast.title: Ill-fated Tour
podcast.body: The Big Bopper performed on the penultimate date of an ill-fated tour, which was attended by a young Robert Zimmerman (Bob Dylan), alongside Buddy Holly and Richie Valens. "He was enough of a fan of Rock and Roll music that he went to see Buddy Holly, Richie Valens, and the Big Bopper, on the penultimate date of their ill-fated tour."

podcast.body: J.P. Richardson died early in 1959 in an infamous Iowa plane crash, an accident that also claimed the lives of Buddy Holly and Ritchie Valens. "J.P. Richardson, better known as the Big Bopper, who died early in 1959 in that infamous Iowa plane crash, that also took the lives of Buddy Holly and Richie Valens."

podcast.title: Songwriter of White Lightning
podcast.body: J.P. Richardson, known as The Big Bopper, wrote George Jones's first country hit, "White Lightning." "It was written by J.P. Richardson, better known as the Big Bopper..."
